To understand the concept of relativity mentioned in the text, imagine time as a river flowing at a steady pace for everyone. In our everyday lives, this river flows at the same speed for you, me, and the person standing next to us. However, Einstein’s theory of relativity suggests that this "river" can actually speed up or slow down depending on how fast you are moving or how strong the gravity is around you.

Think of it like this: Imagine you are running on a treadmill that is moving incredibly fast, almost as fast as light. To you, sitting on the treadmill, everything feels normal. Your watch ticks at its usual rate, and your heart beats at its usual pace. But imagine a friend standing still on the floor next to the treadmill, watching you. From their perspective, because you are moving so incredibly fast, your movements would appear to be in slow motion. Your watch would seem to tick much slower than theirs. This is called "time dilation." It’s not that your watch is broken; it’s that time itself is passing differently for you compared to your stationary friend.

Similarly, gravity can affect time. Imagine gravity as a heavy blanket draped over space. The heavier the object (like a planet or a black hole), the deeper the "dip" in the blanket. Time moves slower in these deeper dips. So, if you were standing near a massive black hole, time would pass more slowly for you than for someone far away in empty space. When you eventually returned to the person who stayed far away, you would have aged less than they had. This isn't science fiction; it's a real phenomenon that GPS satellites have to account for to give you accurate directions!
